title: ORF Resource
description: Schema for resource.json, a reference document (a PDF, an ebook, a paper, slides) in the Open Resource Format (ORF), version 0.1.0. document_url points at wherever the actual file is hosted and is always required as the canonical source. Distinct from OAF: an ORF resource is a document OES doesn't own or render as prose — a genuine written article always belongs in OAF instead. A resource MAY additionally carry a local_path to a bundled copy of the file, for fully offline/portable packages, when downloadable permits it.

$schema.description: Optional. Points an editor (e.g. VS Code) at this document's JSON Schema for inline validation/autocomplete. A JSON-tooling convention, not part of the OES content model — an OES parser ignores it like any other unrecognized field.

orf_version.description: Any 0.1.x patch release of ORF — see the Versioning & Conformance policy for what's allowed to change in a patch.

id.description: Kebab-case. Must match this resource's folder name when co-located (referenced via a `path`).

authors.description: GitHub usernames of the authors. A resource can be hosted and reused independently of any lesson, so it needs its own attribution.

license.description: SPDX license identifier, e.g. "CC-BY-4.0". This describes the resource's own metadata (title, description, table of contents); it does not by itself grant redistribution rights to the underlying document file — see `downloadable`.

document_url.description: Where the actual document is hosted. ORF describes metadata about the document, not the document file itself.

downloadable.description: Whether the file at document_url may be downloaded and redistributed as part of an exported/portable OES package. Only set true when you hold the rights to redistribute the document file itself (self-hosted or appropriately licensed content) — never for a third-party-hosted file where mirroring it would violate that source's terms. Consuming apps must treat the absence of this field, or a value of false, as "do not download and bundle this file".

local_path.description: Filename (no subdirectories), from this resource.json's own folder, to a locally-bundled copy of the document file — present only when an app has already downloaded it (permitted by `downloadable: true`) and included it in this package for offline reading. Author-written resource.json files normally omit this entirely; it's populated by tooling, not hand-authored, and is not meant to be committed to the authoring git repo — see the Offline & Portable Packages guidance for the recommended .gitignore pattern this fixed extension set enables. A consumer that finds the file at this path should prefer reading it over fetching document_url, and fall back to document_url when it's absent or missing.

status.description: Content lifecycle stage. Absent is equivalent to "published" — this field exists for a consumer that wants to hide draft/deprecated content or an author's own tooling, not to gate access by itself.

toc.description: Table of contents — page-anchored sections, so a consuming app can build real chapter navigation instead of a raw page-by-page scroll. Optional; omit for a short document with no natural sections.

references.description: Cited sources — papers, books, or sites this document's content is based on. Each entry is either a bare URL (the simple case) or a richer object — needed for a source with no single URL, like a print book (identified by isbn) or a paper (identified by doi).

related.description: Suggested material for a learner who wants to go further after this specific resource — a related reading, a recommended book, another course. Distinct from references, which documents this resource's own sources rather than suggesting where to go next.

reference.description: A cited source or further-reading pointer.

oneOf.description: Shorthand for a source that's just a URL, nothing more.

url.description: Where to find this source online. Omit entirely for a source with no online location, e.g. a print-only book — isbn/publisher/year identify it instead.

isbn.description: For type: book. ISBN-10 or ISBN-13, digits and optional hyphens.

doi.description: For type: paper. Digital Object Identifier, e.g. "10.1000/xyz123".

note.description: Why this source is included, e.g. "primary source for the historical claims in section 2".

related_item.description: A suggested piece of material for the learner to explore further — distinct from `references`, which documents this content's own sources. Either an OES-native pointer (`path` or one of the `*_url` fields, the same idiom used by every other cross-reference in OES, so a consuming app can fetch it and render it richly — real duration, thumbnail, etc.) or a fully external pointer (a bare `url`) for anything not itself modeled as OES content, e.g. a YouTube video or a book's product page.

type.description: What kind of thing this is, independent of how it's addressed below.

path.description: Path to co-located OES content (a video.json, article.json, set.json, course.json, or resource.json) this entry points at.

url.description: For material not modeled as OES content at all — e.g. a YouTube video, an external article, a book's product page.

content_hash.description: Optional sha256 pin, meaningful only alongside one of the *_url fields.

note.description: Why this is suggested, e.g. "if you want a deeper dive into the underlying math".

source.description: Where this content was originally sourced or adapted from, if it wasn't authored directly for OES — e.g. produced by an importer against another platform's content. Entirely optional; omit for content authored directly. Distinct from this document's own top-level `license`, which describes this OES document's license, not what it was adapted from — the original may be more restrictive (or simply different) and belongs in `source.license` instead. Also distinct from `downloadable`/`local_path`: `source` records provenance, it never by itself grants redistribution rights to the underlying document file.

platform.description: Free-text label for the originating platform or site. Deliberately not an enum — OES doesn't hard-code or endorse any specific platform; any importer fills in whatever's accurate.

license.description: The ORIGINAL content's license or terms of use at the source. Free text, not constrained to SPDX like this document's own `license` field.

retrieved_at.description: When this content was fetched/adapted from the source.

note.description: Free-text context an importer or author wants to record.
